title: Power Pages: Power BI Embed Token v2 support for paginated reports and multi-report embedding
summary: The roadmap facts and cited configuration paths are supported, and the briefing correctly reports the disagreement with Learn about token versions and paginated reports. Hold for a missing qualification: the Apply roles field is available only with Embed for your customers, not every embedding access type.

claims.claim: The roadmap says Power Pages now supports Power BI Embed Token v2.
claims.quote: Power Pages now supports Power BI Embed Token v2

claims.claim: The roadmap describes scenarios that Embed Token v1 did not support.
claims.quote: unlocking modern Power BI embedding scenarios that weren't supported with Embed Token v1.

claims.claim: The roadmap includes paginated reports, including reports using Power BI datasets or requiring multi-resource tokens.
claims.quote: Paginated (RDL) reports, including reports that use Power BI datasets as a data source or require multi-resource tokens.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The roadmap includes data lake-based semantic models requiring dataset and identity permissions in a v2 token.
claims.quote: Reports backed by data lake–based semantic models, where v2 tokens are required to include dataset and identity permissions in the embed token.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: A single v2 token can grant access to multiple reports and datasets according to the roadmap.
claims.quote: Multi‑artifact embedding scenarios, where a single token can grant access to multiple reports and datasets

claims.claim: Makers must use Embed Token v2 to use the roadmap's scenarios.
claims.quote: To use these scenarios, makers must use Embed Token v2 when configuring Power BI embedding in their Power Pages sites.

claims.claim: The roadmap says the feature is enabled by admins, makers or marketers for end users.
claims.quote: Enabled by admins/makers/marketers for end users

claims.claim: The Embedded toggle is at Power Platform admin center > Resources > Power Pages sites > site > Manage > Services > Enable Power BI Embedded.
claims.quote: Under Resources choose Power Pages sites. ... Select Manage from the main menu. ... On the site information page, in the Services section, enable the Enable Power BI Embedded toggle.

claims.claim: No automation equivalent for the site's Power BI integration toggles is documented at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages enable disable Power BI visualization Embedded automation Power Platform API pac pages admin PowerShell Dataverse site settings; Power BI Power Pages Microsoft.PowerApps.Administration.PowerShell. Opened admin/admin-api and set-up-power-bi-integration; read CLI search excerpts.

claims.where: controls[1].ui and controls[1].api; What's changing; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: No Power Pages selector for Embed Token v1 versus v2 is documented on either UI or automation surfaces.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages Power BI embed token version 2 selector Dataverse Web API site setting; Power Pages Embed Token v2. Opened integration, component, Liquid report and admin API pages; read site settings and Generate an embed token search excerpts. No Power Pages selector found.

claims.claim: Enabling or disabling site Power BI integration restarts the website and makes it unavailable for a few minutes.
claims.quote: While Power BI Embedded service is being enabled, the website restarts and is unavailable for a few minutes. ... While Power BI Embedded service is being disabled, the website restarts and is unavailable for a few minutes.

claims.claim: Power BI Visualization has its own site toggle in the Services section.
claims.quote: On the site information page, in the Services section, enable the Power BI Visualization toggle.

claims.claim: Learn names Global administrator for the Power BI Embedded setup.
claims.quote: You must sign in with the same Global administrator account that you used to enable the Power BI Embedded service.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters
claims.claim: The default state of the v2 change on arrival is not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages Power BI Embed Token v2 select version site setting default existing embeds identity licensing pricing; Power Pages Embed Token v2. Read roadmap, integration, component and Liquid report pages. No v2 default or automatic migration statement found.

claims.claim: Power BI Embedded integration requires separately licensed Power BI Embedded capacity, represented as add-on licensing.
claims.quote: To use Power BI Embedded service, you must have an appropriate Power BI Embedded license.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Set up Power BI integration requires an appropriate Power BI licence.
claims.quote: You must have an appropriate Power BI license.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The Power BI Embedded service requires an appropriate Power BI Embedded licence.
claims.quote: To use Power BI Embedded service, you must have an appropriate Power BI Embedded license.

claims.claim: The integration page tells administrators to review Power BI Embedded capacity planning and pricing.
claims.quote: Ensure you review capacity planning, and pricing for Power BI Embedded.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost; Open questions
claims.claim: No separate Power Pages Embed Token v2 licence, meter or price is published at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages Power BI embed token v2 license pricing meter capacity. Opened integration and embedded-capacity; read Power Platform licensing FAQs and Embedded FAQ excerpts. Found existing capacity and website licensing, but no separate Power Pages v2 charge.

claims.claim: Learn still says Power Pages uses version 1 of the Generate token API, unlike the roadmap.
claims.quote: Power Pages uses version 1 of the Generate token API. If any embedded item requires version 2 of the Generate token API, you see this error.

claims.claim: The Add a Power BI component page still says paginated Power BI reports are unsupported.
claims.quote: Paginated Power BI reports aren't supported.

claims.claim: The Liquid report embedding page still says paginated Power BI reports are unsupported.
claims.quote: Paginated Power BI reports are not supported.

claims.claim: Embed for your customers can share reports and dashboards with external users without Power BI licences.
claims.quote: Allows you to securely share the Power BI dashboards or reports to external users without a Power BI license or Microsoft Entra authentication setup.

claims.claim: External viewers using Embed for your customers do not need Microsoft Entra authentication setup.
claims.quote: Allows you to securely share the Power BI dashboards or reports to external users without a Power BI license or Microsoft Entra authentication setup.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Anyone can view a dashboard embedded with Embed for your customers on an anonymously accessible webpage.
claims.quote: If you add Power BI with Embed for your customers on a webpage that's available anonymously, anyone can view the dashboard.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Page permissions are the documented control for securing the page carrying customer-embedded content.
claims.quote: To secure this page, read Page permissions in Power Pages.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Reports with Power BI roles must have those roles entered in Apply roles, without restricting that instruction to an access type.
claims.quote: Apply roles: If you have defined roles in Power BI and assigned them to reports, you must enter the appropriate roles in this field. ... This option is only available for the access type Embed for your customers.
claims.fix: Add the qualification 'For the Embed for your customers access type' to the Apply roles instruction and to the checklist instruction to test passed roles. Microsoft documents Apply roles only for that access type at https://learn.microsoft.com/power-pages/getting-started/add-power-bi.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Learn lists missing passed RLS roles as a cause of the report rendering configuration error.
claims.quote: A configuration error occurred while rendering your report. ... Row-level security in Power BI is enabled, but roles aren't passed in the Power BI component configuration (Advanced settings), or in the roles parameter in the powerbi liquid tag.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Embed content in apps must be enabled or the portal cannot render embedded Power BI reports or dashboards.
claims.quote: Ensure that Embed content in apps is Enabled in your Power BI tenant Developer settings. When disabled, a portal can't render embedded Power BI dashboards or reports.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Learn associates the model schema error with embedding an item requiring Generate token API v2.
claims.quote: Couldn't load the model schema associated with this report. Make sure you have a connection to the server, and try again. ... If any embedded item requires version 2 of the Generate token API, you see this error.

claims.claim: The roadmap and relevant Learn pages describe embedding and viewing rather than autonomous behaviour.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages Embed Token v2. Read the complete roadmap description and integration, component and Liquid report pages. These describe embedding, authentication, report configuration and viewing; no autonomous feature behaviour was described.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented whether this v2 change automatically changes existing Power Pages embeds.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages Power BI Embed Token v2 select version site setting default existing embeds identity licensing pricing; Power Pages Embed Token v2. Read roadmap, integration, component and Liquid report pages. No existing-embed migration statement found.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: The Power Pages-specific identity mapping for the new data lake-backed v2 scenario is not described.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages Power BI Embed Token v2 select version site setting default existing embeds identity licensing pricing. Read integration setup and Generate an embed token excerpts. General token identities are documented, but no Power Pages v2 data lake identity mapping was found.

claims.claim: For customer-embedded paginated reports using a Power BI semantic model, both items must be in Premium per capacity or Embedded workspaces.
claims.quote: The paginated report and the Power BI semantic model must reside in a Premium per capacity or Embedded workspace (they can reside in two different workspaces).

claims.claim: Power BI visualization must be enabled on the site to embed Power BI content.
claims.quote: To view dashboards and reports from Power BI on webpages on a website, you must enable Power BI visualization from the Power Platform admin center.

claims.claim: Embed for your customers requires the Power BI Embedded service enabled and the relevant workspaces selected.
claims.quote: Ensure Power BI Embedded service is enabled and respective Power BI workspaces are selected and shared with the maker or the logged-in user.

claims.claim: Makers can add Power BI components or Liquid tags to Power Pages webpages.
claims.quote: This article explains how to add a Power BI report or dashboard using powerbi Liquid tag. To add Power BI component on a webpage in your website using the design studio, go to Add a Power BI component.

claims.claim: The Power Pages admin API page lists site start, stop, WAF and visibility operations but no Power BI operation.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages enable disable Power BI visualization Embedded automation Power Platform API pac pages admin PowerShell Dataverse site settings. Opened https://learn.microsoft.com/power-pages/admin/admin-api and read its complete operations table: start, stop, WAF and visibility, no Power BI.

claims.claim: Managing Power BI developer settings requires a Fabric administrator.
claims.quote: To manage Power BI developer settings, you must be a Fabric administrator.

claims.claim: Developer tenant settings are configured at OneLake catalog > Govern > Configurations > Tenant settings.
claims.quote: These settings are configured in OneLake catalog > Govern > Configurations > Tenant settings.

claims.where: Scope; Cost and licensing; Open questions
claims.claim: Additional requirements specific to Power Pages v2, beyond documented surrounding-product requirements, are not published.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages Embed Token v2; Power Pages Power BI embed token v2 license pricing meter capacity. Read integration, component, paginated embedding and capacity pages. General embedding prerequisites exist; no Power Pages v2-specific prerequisite list found.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented whether v2 support resolves the model schema error on existing Power Pages pages.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages Embed Token v2; Power Pages Power BI Embed Token v2 select version site setting default existing embeds identity licensing pricing. Read integration troubleshooting and roadmap. Neither states the effect on existing pages showing the error.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout and At rollout
claims.claim: Checklist instructions to check page permissions, Embed content in apps, capacity and passed RLS roles lack corresponding controls-table rows.
claims.quote: Checklist: 'Check that anonymous pages ... have the page permissions you intend'; 'Confirm ... Embed content in apps is Enabled and ... capacity'; 'Test that row-level security roles are passed'. Table: site Power BI enablement and token version only.
claims.fix: The Before rollout page-permissions and tenant-setting/capacity checks, and the At rollout passed-roles check, have no table rows. Remove those three checklist bullets; retain the supported explanatory coverage elsewhere. Do not add unverified control rows as part of this correction.

controlChecks.governs: Whether Power BI visualization and the Power BI Embedded service are enabled on a site
